Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we move toward a procurement packet, procurement has asked for granular sizing guidance so they can justify the reserved spend to finance. High level: we expect a steady-state of 75k inferences/day (avg payload ~800 tokens) and a 99th percentile burst up to 22k qps during batch imports. Latency SLO is soft 300ms p95 but some daytime endpoints need p99 < 650ms.

Can you provide:
- recommended GPU family mix (A100, H100, or an infer-focused ampere variant) for a mix of real-time chat (few-shot prompts) and batch transforms
- throughput per-GPU and suggested reservation counts for a committed pool (targeting 3 months runway)
- fallback strategy if reserved capacity is exhausted (model variants, region fallback, pre-emptible burst)
- an attachmentable workbook we can include in procurement packet (throughput math + cost delta rows)

If you can get something by Wed morning PT that would line up with our review.

Appreciate it,
Carlos

Carlos — thanks for the clear ask. I put together a concise playbook and attached a workbook that walks through assumptions and reservation counts. High level summary below; workbook attached (amaris_throughput_workbook_v1.xlsx) includes per-GPU throughput curves, cost delta table, and a sensitivity sheet for token length.

High-level recommendation (short):
- Baseline: 50% H100 (dense float16 for high latency-sensitive chat paths), 40% A100-80GB (quantized variants for batch/transform), 10% T4/Low-cost inference nodes for low-priority background jobs
- Per-GPU throughput: H100 ~ 1,100 qps (avg 800-token few-shot chat, p95 latency ~240ms when served single-tenant on Redwood Dedicated), A100 (q4_quant) ~ 420 qps for larger batches, T4 ~ 75 qps for tiny micro-batches
- Reservation counts (3-month runway, target steady-state + 30% burst headroom): 18 H100, 36 A100, 6 T4 (workbook shows math)
- Fallback: priority routing to quantized model (A100/q4) for real-time endpoints when H100 capacity hits 85%; automated regional fallback to our secondary region in east with identical model variants; short-lived burst on dedicated pre-emptible pool for bulk imports with FIFO admission and graceful backpressure

Key tradeoffs and notes:
- H100s deliver superior p99 tail for few-shot chat but at ~2.2x cost/unit vs optimized A100 q4. We recommend mixing to keep costs predictable while preserving conversational latency for paid/consumer-facing endpoints.
- Quantization and prefix caching will materially move batch economics; workbook includes a modeled 18–27% token-cost reduction under caching assumptions.
- For compliance/audit trails, Dedicated provides tenant-level audit logs and can be scoped to cover your HIPAA evidence requests — if Amaris wants the private control plane, we can add KMS/HSM integration notes in a follow-up.

Next steps I propose:
1) Review the attached workbook with your finance/procurement team (I can join Wed 11am PT)
2) If counts look off, we run a short synthetic runbook (48h) on a small sample of your payload to validate throughput curves before procurement commit
3) Draft a mutual action plan for the reserved PO including stage gates for burst capacity and fallback thresholds

Sending the workbook now — le me know a good time to sync.

Best,
Soojin Lee

Looping in a brief alternative that has helped similar healthcare customers reduce committed dollars while protecting SLAs:

Alternative GPU mix (cost-constrained):
- 30% H100, 60% A100-q4, 10% T4 (shift more work to aggressively quantized variants with tuned kernels)
- Reservation counts (same runway): 12 H100, 48 A100, 6 T4
- Operational guardrails: strict rollout gating (canary at 1–2% traffic), active quality monitoring with automatic rollback on eval regressions

Rationale: when customers can tolerate a modest p99 drift (300–400ms additional tail) we can reduce H100s by ~33% and add A100 quantized capacity for throughput. This lowers committed spend ~27% in the workbook model.

If Amaris has endpoints that are revenue-sensitive (chat triage with clinicians), mark those as H100-only in the routing policy — others can be on the quantized path. Happy to walk the math in Wed's call.

-Marcus
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference

Carlos — attaching the two items you requested. Quick extracts below and I've added the single-line numbers into the workbook summary tab for procurement: 

Monthly committed cost (baseline mix): $138,400 per month
Monthly committed cost (cost-constrained alternative): $101,200 per month
Estimated delta: $37,200 per month (baseline -> alternative) — workbook includes amortized support and reserved discounts.

Ordered fallback matrix (high to low priority):
1) Route to quantized A100 variant (q4) for CPU-equivalent tokens — expected p95 +20–50ms, p99 +120–180ms vs H100 baseline
2) Regional fallback to secondary east cluster (identical model variants) — expected p95 +40–80ms, p99 +200–300ms depending on cross-region network egress; works if your endpoints accept slight increase in observed latency
3) Degrade to cached-response policy for non-fresh queries (prefix/KV cache) — p95 unaffected for cache hits, p99 effectively controlled for those endpoints but reduces freshness for low-priority requests
4) Short-lived burst on pre-emptible dedicated pool with admission control (bulk imports only) — p95/p99 vary; workbook shows expected throughput but we recommend only for batch imports with retry/backoff

Synthetic runbook: we only need anonymized payloads (no PHI). Minimal fields: tokenized prompt length distribution, sample few-shot prompts, and a 24h traffic slice (gzipped NDJSON) — we provide a script that strips identifiers. The runbook can be done under a mutual NDA and we will run it inside your VPC if you prefer.

Next steps: I can join your procurement call Thu EOD or Fri morning PT to walk the workbook and fallback matrix. If you approve the workbook language, Marcus will draft the MSA/reservation term sheet.

Cheers,
